from.place: Proof paragraph 2, middle derived mapping-complex comparison before the inverse limit: coherent monadic bar foundation, conditional free-module criterion; Higher Algebra (2017), Definition 4.2.1.1, Notation 4.2.1.6, Definitions 4.2.1.7, 4.2.1.13 and 4.2.1.19, Remark 4.2.1.21; Corollary 4.2.3.2; proof of Proposition 4.2.4.2, the operad LM_0 and its algebra category.

title: Module operad and algebra-plus-object restriction
statement:
Use quasicategories and coherent functor categories of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], inner, cocartesian and cartesian fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], monoidal infinity-categories of [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category], the ordinary category $\mathsf{LM}^\otimes$ of pointed maps with ordered fibres, its nerve $N(\mathsf{LM}^\otimes)$ (written $L$ there and $\mathrm{LM}^\otimes$ here) and pure-algebra part $A$, operadic fibrations, inert arrows, coherent left tensorings, associative algebras as inert-preserving sections over $A$, module objects as inert-preserving sections over $\mathrm{LM}^\otimes$, and $\operatorname{LMod}_B(\mathcal M)$ with its underlying-object functor $U$, all as in [def-coef-left-module-operadic-encoding], and the symmetric infinity-operads, active arrows and algebra categories defined in [lem-coef-relative-operadic-terminal-active-mapping]. Let $\mathcal V$ be any monoidal infinity-category and $\mathcal M$ any infinity-category coherently left-tensored over $\mathcal V$ in the sense of [def-coef-left-module-operadic-encoding], that is, by an operadic fibration $q:\mathcal E^\otimes\to\mathrm{LM}^\otimes$ which is cocartesian over all arrows, with colour fibres $\mathcal E_a=\mathcal V$ and $\mathcal E_m=\mathcal M$.

Regard $\mathrm{LM}^\otimes$ over $N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)$ by forgetting the fibre orders. In the colored-operad language of the definition: an operation to $a$ is a linear ordering of its inputs, all of color $a$ (the empty list is allowed); an operation to $m$ is a linear ordering with exactly one input of color $m$, at the end, and all preceding inputs of color $a$; substitution concatenates the ordered lists. Thus a morphism $(\langle n\rangle,S)\to(\langle n\prime\rangle,S\prime)$ carries $S\cup\{*\}$ into $S\prime\cup\{*\}$, and its fibre over each element of $S\prime$ contains exactly one element of $S$, last in its order. Let $\mathrm{LM}_0^\otimes$ be the subcategory spanned by all objects and those morphisms $\alpha:(\langle n\rangle,S)\to(\langle n\prime\rangle,S\prime)$ with no $a$-input over any $m$-output: for every $s\prime\in S\prime$, the fiber $\alpha^{-1}(\{s\prime\})$ is a singleton, necessarily of color $m$. Equivalently, $\alpha^{-1}(S\prime)\subseteq S$; inputs sent to the basepoint are unrestricted. Write $i:\mathrm{LM}_0^\otimes\hookrightarrow\mathrm{LM}^\otimes$ for its inclusion. Its operations with output $m$ are only the unary identity, while its restriction to the $a$-color is the associative operad.

Composed with $\mathrm{LM}^\otimes\to N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)$, $\mathcal E^\otimes$ is an infinity-operad and $q$ is a cocartesian fibration of infinity-operads in the sense of [lem-coef-relative-operadic-terminal-active-mapping]; $\mathrm{LM}^\otimes$ and $\mathrm{LM}_0^\otimes$ are small infinity-operads and $i$ preserves inert edges. Transport over an ordered operation $a^r\to a$ is the $r$-fold tensor product, including the tensor unit for $r=0$, and transport over $a^r,m\to m$ is the iterated left action. There are coherent equivalences
$$\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathrm{LM}/\mathrm{LM}}(\mathcal E)\simeq\operatorname{LMod}(\mathcal M),\qquad \operatorname{Alg}_{\mathrm{LM}_0/\mathrm{LM}}(\mathcal E)\simeq\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal V)\times\mathcal M.$$
Here $\operatorname{LMod}(\mathcal M)$ is the infinity-category of module objects of [def-coef-left-module-operadic-encoding]: inert-preserving sections $\mathrm{LM}^\otimes\to\mathcal E^\otimes$, written as pairs $(B,L)$ of their restriction $B$ to $A$ and their value $L$ at $m$, with algebra-changing transformations over $\mathrm{LM}^\otimes$ and their higher simplices; the first equivalence is the identification of inert-preserving functors over $\mathrm{LM}^\otimes$ with these sections. Restriction along $i$ is $(B,L)\mapsto(B,UL)$. These equivalences preserve both coordinates, transformations and all parameter simplices. Projection $\Theta:\operatorname{LMod}(\mathcal M)\to\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal V)$ is a cartesian fibration, and its degreewise fiber over $B$ is $\operatorname{LMod}_B(\mathcal M)$ of [def-coef-left-module-operadic-encoding]. No presentability or colimit hypothesis is required.

source.place: Higher Algebra (2017), Definition 4.2.1.1, Notation 4.2.1.6, Definitions 4.2.1.7, 4.2.1.13 and 4.2.1.19, Remark 4.2.1.21; Corollary 4.2.3.2; proof of Proposition 4.2.4.2, the operad LM_0 and its algebra category. The LM_0 condition is written explicitly by its output fibers, correcting the ill-typed inverse-image display in that proof in accordance with its Assoc coproduct Triv identification. Online source rechecked during repair; WANTED: archive in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text: First check the ordinary operators. The operation to $a$ consists entirely of $a$ inputs with a chosen order, and the operation to $m$ consists of ordered $a$ inputs followed by its unique $m$ input, exactly as in [def-coef-left-module-operadic-encoding]. Substitution preserves this description: replacing an $a$ input inserts only $a$ inputs; replacing the last $m$ input inserts $a$ inputs followed by one last $m$. The empty algebra list gives the unit, whereas there is no nullary operation to $m$. For $\mathrm{LM}_0$, substituting into an $m$ output only substitutes a unary $m$ identity into a unary $m$ identity. Thus its operators are closed under composition and identities. The equivalence of its two membership tests follows because every module-output fibre already contains its unique module input: it has no algebra input precisely when it is that singleton. Discarding to $*$ is unrestricted. Every inert operator has singleton identity operations at each retained output, so lies in $\mathrm{LM}_0$. The sets of finite tuples, pointed maps and fibre orders are small in the chosen universe.

source.place: Definitions 4.2.1.1 and 4.2.1.7, Notation 4.2.1.6; LM_0 in proof of Proposition 4.2.4.2, corrected fibre condition.

proof.text: Check the infinity-operad axioms of [lem-coef-relative-operadic-terminal-active-mapping] directly for both nerves. A fibre over $\langle n\rangle$ is the discrete set of $n$ color choices, hence the $n$-fold product of the color fibre, including its unique empty tuple. A map over a fixed pointed map is exactly the product of the independently chosen output operations. Inert lifts retain their selected colors and use their unary identities. They are cocartesian: precomposing an operation with such a selection just relabels its retained inputs, giving a bijection with operations over the composite; the discarded inputs are discarded on both sides. Nerves of the ordinary operator functors are inner fibrations: an inner horn determines the missing composite and the functor preserves that composite. These observations prove all three axioms and show $i$ preserves inert edges. For $\mathcal E^\otimes\to N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)$, lift an inner horn first to $\mathrm{LM}^\otimes$ and then by $q$; its Segal fibre decomposition is the disjoint union, over color tuples, of the product decompositions supplied by [def-coef-left-module-operadic-encoding]. Its mapping-space decomposition is obtained by grouping each $q$-mapping fibre by its underlying pointed map and then its output operations. Products distribute over these independent disjoint choices. A $q$-cocartesian lift of an inert LM operator is cocartesian for the composite projection as well: its mapping square over Fin_* is obtained by the $q$-cocartesian mapping square of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] on each LM-operator component and the relabeling bijection just checked. Conversely, for an inert operator the same componentwise square detects $q$-cocartesianness. Therefore $q$ preserves inert edges and is the required cocartesian fibration and map of infinity-operads. Its transports are the ordered tensor and action functors in the definition, including the nullary algebra unit.

By the definition of relative algebra categories in [lem-coef-relative-operadic-terminal-active-mapping], an LM/LM algebra is an inert-preserving functor whose composite with $q$ is the identity of LM. This is literally a section, with the same transformations and parameter simplices as in [def-coef-left-module-operadic-encoding]. Thus the first equivalence is an identification. For the second use [lem-coef-colored-operation-section-reconstruction], applied to $q$ pulled back to LM_0; its hypotheses follow from Step 2 and the given cocartesian lifts, which restrict to the pullback. Given $B\in\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal V)$ and $x\in\mathcal M$, assign $B$ to color $a$ and $x$ to color $m$. The structure arrows at all $a$ operations are precisely those of $B$; the sole $m$ operation is the unary identity of $x$. Every tree ending at $a$ is entirely an algebra tree. A tree ending at $m$ is a chain of unary $m$ identities, so its coherences are the identity coherences. There are no trees mixing these two sorts. The reconstruction lemma assembles these data to a section. Restricting a section recovers $B$ and $x$, and the reconstruction identifies the composite with that section. The same construction on a parameter $K$ gives exactly a $K$-family of algebra objects and an independent functor $K\to\mathcal M$. Consequently it proves the equivalence of infinity-categories, including transformations, rather than just a correspondence on objects.

source.place: Definition 4.2.1.13 and proof of Proposition 4.2.4.2; explicit outputwise reconstruction in place of invoking the coproduct theorem as an uncited black box.

proof.text: Restriction along $i$ retains every algebra operation and forgets all nonunary module-action operators; the only module operation remaining in LM_0 is its unary identity. Hence the equivalence of Step 3 sends a module section to $(B,UL)$. The reconstruction is compatible with projection to colors and with every simplicial parameter by [lem-coef-colored-operation-section-reconstruction], so this assertion holds on all transformations and higher simplices. In particular restriction to the full pure-algebra part $A$ is precisely $\Theta$. By [def-coef-left-module-operadic-encoding] its degreewise fibre over the specified algebra section $B$ is $\operatorname{LMod}_B(\mathcal M)$, and evaluation at $m$ is $U$.

source.place: Definition 4.2.1.13; proof of Proposition 4.2.4.2, identification of the two restriction coordinates.

proof.text: The functor $\Theta$ is an inner fibration. Indeed $A\hookrightarrow\mathrm{LM}^\otimes$ is a simplicial monomorphism and $q$ is a categorical fibration by [def-coef-left-module-operadic-encoding]. The exponential corner map of [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation], pulled back over the identity LM diagram, gives an inner fibration from all sections to all pure-algebra sections. Restrict to the full subcategories on inert-preserving sections. In an inner horn of dimension at least two every vertex is present; therefore a lift in all sections has exactly the given inert-preserving vertices and lies in the full subcategory. These full subcategories are quasicategories, since their inner horn fillers have the same vertices. This proves the inner lifting assertion for the actual simplicial restriction functor, without replacing its fibres by a different model.

source.place: Definition 4.2.1.13 (categorical restriction); inner-fibration check by exponential corner and fullness.

proof.text: Let $h:B\to C$ be an algebra transformation and $(C,L)$ a module section. Apply [lem-coef-module-scalar-restriction-coherence] to its ordered operations. It supplies the full coherent system on $UL$ with $B$-operations $b^{h^*L}_r=b^L_r\circ(h^{\otimes r}\otimes1_{UL})$, including the unit and all tree-contraction comparisons, and the compatible transformation data $(h,1_{UL})$. By [lem-coef-colored-operation-section-reconstruction], these systems assemble into a module section $(B,h^*L)$ and an edge $e_h:(B,h^*L)\to(C,L)$. The pure-algebra restriction is $h$ and the module component is the identity, since reconstruction preserves these coordinates and all parameter simplices. Thus this gives a lift with every prescribed target; its cartesianness is checked next.

source.place: Corollary 4.2.3.2, scalar-restriction lift expanded operation by operation; coherence supplied by general colored reconstruction.

proof.text: For a test module $(D,N)$, consider the postcomposition square for $e_h$ over $h\circ-:\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal V)}(D,B)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal V)}(D,C)$. By [lem-coef-module-scalar-restriction-mapping], the operation data of maps into $(B,h^*L)$ over $g$ are equivalent to those of maps into $(C,L)$ over $hg$, naturally over the entire algebra mapping space. Its forward comparison reconstructs to composition with $e_h$. The parameterized transformation clause of [lem-coef-colored-operation-section-reconstruction] therefore identifies the top left corner with the pullback of the other mapping spaces. Step 5 and [lem-coef-infinity-inner-mapping-fiber] make the vertical mapping-space maps Kan fibrations; [lem-coef-kan-pullback-path-comparison] identifies this pullback with the homotopy pullback, retaining coherent identifications of algebra coordinates. The opposite of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] now makes $e_h$ cartesian in the horn sense. Since Step 6 constructs such a lift with any prescribed target and Step 5 makes $\Theta$ inner, [def-coef-infinity-fibrations] gives that $\Theta$ is a cartesian fibration. No presentability or colimit hypothesis has entered.

source.place: Corollary 4.2.3.2, cartesian universal property of scalar restriction; direct mapping-space proof.

proof_origin.place: Definitions 4.2.1.1-19, Corollary 4.2.3.2 and proof of Proposition 4.2.4.2, expanded by operation reconstruction and scalar-restriction mapping comparison. Higher Algebra is online reference material, not archived in literature/.
